title: Contrast-aware token interpolation for dynamic-brand themes and density-specific component overrides
creator: Marina Chen
description: Add a small, focused system for interpolating theme tokens per-brand and per-density so components (buttons, tables, charts, and icons) adapt contrast and saturation predictably in dark and dim modes. This ticket scopes the token interpolation model, component override rules, and an accessibility-first fallback chain. The goal is to reduce manual overrides across brand forks, preserve minimum contrast in tight density variants, avoid color clipping in deep dark backgrounds, and provide a developer-facing mapping table consumed by the runtime style system.
acceptance_criteria: Design token interpolation spec drafted and reviewed by PM/Design/Accessibility
Mapping table that translates brand core palettes into dark/dim token sets for: surface, ink, accent, chart-stroke, and table-border
Per-component override rules defined for button states, table zebra rows, chart series fills, and icon strokes with density modifiers (compact, comfortable)
Automated contrast test vectors (small text, large text, UI controls) included and pass WCAG AA for primary flows or have documented trade-offs
Figma library file with example variants and component instances for each brand + density combination
Implementation notes handed to engineering with token keys and expected CSS/custom properties naming conventions
implementation_notes: Introduce interpolation layer: token.dynamic.interpolate(brandPalette, mode, density) => canonical tokens
Prefer perceptual color space (Oklab) for interpolation to avoid hue shifts in darkening

Define minContrast thresholds per token role (primary/secondary/icon/disabled). If interpolation yields below threshold, apply controlled desaturation + lightness shift rather than blanket brightening
Provide a small set of tunable knobs in token metadata: 'contrastPriority', 'toneAnchor', 'saturationClamp'
Component overrides should opt into token roles (e.g., button.fill uses token.role('accent.surface')), avoid hard-coded color references
Table zebra rule: use surface-layer token with 2% lightness delta in comfortable, 1% in compact; if below contrast threshold, fallback to accent-muted token
Charts: map brand series by 'seriesHueIndex' to ensure readable stroke/fill pairs; provide stroke-first default with fill fallback under low-contrast conditions
Expose mapping table as JSON consumed by console-frontend runtime; keys must be flat (e.g., --rdw-token-accent-300) with additional suffixes for density (--compact)

risks: Brand palettes with extreme saturations may produce unreadable tokens even after interpolation, requiring per-brand manual tuning
Too many per-component overrides will create maintenance burden; aim for token-led overrides instead of component-level hacks
Runtime adoption risk if frontend team cannot map flattened keys to internal style system quickly
Accessibility regressions on edge-case density + language combos (long labels) if not exhaustively tested
